subject: old television set
title: What If You Sat Too Close to the TV? The Warning Had a Real Cause

scenes.text: What if you sat right up against the TV? Your parents' warning came from a real scandal.
In 1967, some large General Electric colour TVs were found leaking X-rays from a faulty tube inside.
About ninety thousand sets had to be fixed, and in 1968 the US passed a law to limit radiation from electronics.
Modern screens don't do that. Eye doctors say sitting close doesn't damage your eyes.
The worst you'll get is tired, strained eyes, and a short break fixes it.
Kids sit close because they can focus up close better than adults. But if one always needs to, check their eyes.

description:
What if you sat too close to the TV? In 1967, about 90,000 GE colour TVs were fixed after leaking X-rays, which led to the 1968 Radiation Control for Health and Safety Act.
Today, the American Academy of Ophthalmology says sitting close doesn't damage the eyes; at worst it causes eye strain.
